stories.title: GLM-5.2 beats Claude in cyber benchmarks, marking a step change for open agents
stories.rationale: Major open-model capability milestone with concrete benchmark and enterprise post-training signal, high-engagement.
stories.summary: Semgrep reports that GLM-5.2 outperforms Claude on its cyber benchmarks, while Interconnects frames the model as a capability threshold for open agentic use. Observers note rising enterprise interest in securing compute to post-train models on top of GLM-5.2.

stories.title: OpenAI reports internal Codex output token growth: 56x Research, 32x Support, 27x Engineering, 13x Legal
stories.rationale: Concrete enterprise/agentic adoption numbers from a primary-adjacent source, directly matching reader interests.
stories.summary: OpenAI reportedly disclosed that median internal Codex output tokens grew 56x in Research, 32x in Customer Support, 27x in Engineering, and 13x in Legal since November 2025. The figures point to rapidly scaling internal agentic coding usage across functions.

stories.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) released to trusted partners
stories.rationale: Major model release, though tiered/restricted and reported via newsletter rather than primary blog.
stories.summary: OpenAI reportedly rolled out a tiered GPT-5.6 family codenamed Sol, Terra, and Luna, restricted to trusted partners. The release coincided with a same-day Anthropic update.

stories.title: Claude becomes a persistent org-wide agent in Slack (Claude Tag)
stories.rationale: Notable agent-harness/UX shift for enterprise workflows, echoed by Karpathy's commentary.
stories.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Tag, enabling multiplayer, proactive, and persistent agents inside Slack. Karpathy describes this as a third major LLM UX paradigm where the model acts as a self-contained asynchronous entity working alongside teams.

stories.title: Agent harnesses go mainstream: meta-harnesses, local coding agents, and open agent clouds
stories.rationale: Directly targets agentic SDLC tooling and evals the reader prioritizes.
stories.summary: Multiple pieces explore the agent-harness ecosystem, from meta-harnesses and Databricks' case for open agent clouds to running open-weight models in local coding harnesses as Claude Code/Codex alternatives. IBM's CUGA also ships two dozen working agentic app examples on a lightweight harness.

stories.title: AI compute economics: SpaceX as a $28B/yr neocloud and xAI renting out its cluster
stories.rationale: Compute/datacenter business dynamics with numbers, though analysis-driven and partly punditry.
stories.summary: Analysis pegs SpaceX as already a $28B/yr neocloud, highlighting the scale of compute as a business. Separately, LeCun argues xAI now rents out its large cluster to rivals because it cannot staff a frontier lab after founder departures.

stories.title: Debate over AI regulation: frontier APIs vs open-weight models and data-center backlash
stories.rationale: Substantive policy debate on open vs closed regulation relevant to infra/enterprise, but opinion-heavy.
stories.summary: Commentators argue frontier API models should be regulated for transparency while open-weight models stay unregulated, warning that regulatory capture could harm competitiveness. Related posts frame the data-center backlash as a proxy for broader anti-AI sentiment.

stories.title: Open-weight ecosystem expands with Zyphra, Cohere, and Poolside releases
stories.rationale: Survey of new open artifacts relevant to model-release tracking.
stories.summary: Interconnects assesses the latest open-weight artifacts from Zyphra, Cohere, and Poolside. The piece examines the breadth of the ecosystem and the motivations behind releasing these models.

stories.title: AI in medicine: Claude Code MRI second-opinion and a Nature cardiac-arrest study
stories.rationale: Concrete applied-AI examples, one peer-reviewed primary source, one anecdotal.
stories.summary: A widely-discussed post describes using Claude Code with Opus to get a second opinion on an MRI, while a Nature paper applies AI to sudden cardiac death prediction. Together they illustrate growing applied medical AI use cases.

stories.title: AI security and red-teaming beyond traditional cybersecurity
stories.rationale: Substantive on AI security/evals, but interview format from a secondary source.
stories.summary: Zico Kolter and Matt Fredrikson of Gray Swan argue AI security is distinct from applying AI to cybersecurity. The discussion covers red-teaming frontier models after the Mythos benchmark.
